questions.question: A capacity constraint reads $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought. What does the term $50y$ represent?
options: The purchase cost of the machine, paid when $y=1$
The extra capacity, counted only when the machine is bought
The capacity that is lost when the machine is bought
The production of the new machine, which always equals $50$

questions.question: Is the constraint $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought, a linear constraint in the variables $x_1,x_2,y$?
options: No: a variable on the right-hand side makes it nonlinear
Yes: its right-hand side is a linear expression in $y$
No: $y$ multiplies the capacity, which is a product of terms
Yes, but only after fixing $y$ to one value in advance

questions.question: Products 1 and 2 are made on the same production line, which has $100$ units of capacity; buying an extra machine for that line adds $50$. With binary $y$ for the purchase, why does the model use one constraint on $x_1+x_2$?
options: Both products use one shared capacity, which limits the total
Each product separately may use the full capacity of the line
Both products sell at the same price, so only their total matters
The total must equal the capacity whenever $y$ equals $1$

questions.question: A planner adds the constraint $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought, and the machine costs $60$. Where must the cost $60$ appear for the model to account for it?
options: Nowhere: the capacity constraint already contains the cost
On the right-hand side, as $100+50y-60$ in the capacity
As a constraint $x_1+x_2\ge60y$, so that sales cover the cost
In the objective, e.g. as $-60y$, or in a budget limit

questions.question: A workshop has $80$ hours of capacity per week; an extra shift, decided by the binary $y$ ($y=1$: shift scheduled), adds $30$ hours. The constraint is $x_1+x_2\le80+30y$ for the hours $x_1,x_2$ of two jobs. What are the weekly limits for $y=0$ and $y=1$?
options: $0$ hours and $110$ hours
$80$ hours and $30$ hours
$110$ hours and $80$ hours
$80$ hours and $110$ hours

questions.question: For the constraint $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought, is the plan $(x_1,x_2)=(60,70)$ feasible?
options: With $y=0$ already, as $130$ is at most $150$
With neither value, as $130$ exceeds $100+50$
Only with $y=1$, as the total $130$ exceeds $100$
With either value, since $y$ does not limit $x_1$

questions.question: Machine hours are limited by $3x_1+x_2\le120+30y$, where $y\in\{0,1\}$ and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought. For which values of $y$ is the plan $(x_1,x_2)=(20,60)$ feasible?
options: Both: it needs $120$ hours, within either limit
Only $y=1$: $120$ is not strictly below the limit $120$
Neither: it needs $200$ hours, above $150$
Only $y=0$: the extra $30$ hours are not needed

questions.question: Existing capacity is $100$ and an extra machine, bought when the binary $y$ equals $1$, adds $50$. A student writes $x_1+x_2\le150y$. What is wrong with this constraint?
options: With $y=0$ it forbids all production, losing the old $100$
With $y=1$ it allows only $50$, the machine's capacity alone
Nothing: for both values of $y$ it equals $100+50y$
It is not linear, since $150$ multiplies the variable $y$

questions.question: A model uses $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with only the bounds $0\le y\le1$ for the purchase variable $y$ (where $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought). What can the solution then contain?
options: Only $y=0$ or $y=1$, since the bounds already exclude fractions
Only $y=1$, since the upper bound $1$ is always reached
Only $y=0$, since a fraction of a machine has no cost
A value such as $y=0.4$: capacity $120$ from part of a machine

questions.question: A profit model contains $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought, but no purchase cost of the machine anywhere. What does this imply for the optimal $y$?
options: $y=0$ is always optimal, since buying is a cost to avoid
$y=1$ is optimal only if the extra capacity is fully used
$y=1$ is never worse, as it only enlarges the feasible set
$y$ has no effect, since it does not appear in the objective

questions.question: Solve $\max\ 3x_1+2x_2-60y$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$, $x_1\le80$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ and $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $60$ is the cost of an extra machine. What is the optimal value?

A model allows at most one of two machines: $x_1+x_2\le100+50y_1+80y_2$ and $y_1+y_2\le1$, with $y_1,y_2\in\{0,1\}$ and $y_j=1$ meaning machine $j$ is bought. Which capacities for $x_1+x_2$ can the model choose?
options: $150$ and $180$ only
$100$ and $230$ only

questions.question: Capacity is $100$, and at least $140$ units must be produced. Machine A adds $30$ (cost $40$), B adds $50$ (cost $70$), C adds $15$ (cost $20$); each can be bought once. Which purchase meets the requirement at the lowest cost?
options: A alone, for $40$
B alone, for $70$
A and C, for $60$
B and C, for $90$

questions.question: A profit model has the constraint $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought, a cost term $-Ky$ with $K>0$ in the objective, and $y$ appears nowhere else. If an optimal solution has $y=1$, what must hold for its plan?
options: $x_1+x_2=150$, as the bought capacity is always used up
$x_1+x_2>100$, or else $y=0$ would give a higher profit
Nothing, as $y=1$ is allowed for every feasible plan
$x_1+x_2\le100$, as the extra machine is a reserve

questions.question: For the constraint $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $x_1,x_2$ are production quantities sharing the capacity and $y=1$ means an extra machine is bought, which implication does the constraint itself enforce?
options: Buying forces the total above $100$; a large total does not force $y$
A total above $100$ forces $y=1$; buying forces nothing
Both: $y=1$ holds exactly when the total exceeds $100$
Neither: $y$ may be chosen independently of the plan

questions.question: Solve the purchase decision for $\max\ 4x_1+3x_2-Ky$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le100+50y$, $x_1\le120$, $x_2\le10$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, $y\in\{0,1\}$, where $K$ is the machine cost. For which costs $K$ is buying strictly better?
options: For $K<110$
For $K<200$
For $K<150$
For $K<80$
